purpose: Compile, step, and replay an explicit deterministic state/event graph for games, workflows, interfaces, tools, or simulations without evaluating code or inventing missing transitions.

properties.operation: compile by default, step, or replay
properties.machine: axm.deterministic-state-machine/v0.1 object with explicit states and unique state/event transitions
properties.state: current state for step or optional replay start override

relationships: returns explicit transition effects as inert JSON data
holds on an undeclared state/event pair instead of guessing a rule

anatomy_refs.basis: Compiles and executes a closed deterministic state/event transition component.
Provides bounded compile, single-step, and replay runtime operations without arbitrary code evaluation.

limitations: transition effects are inert JSON outputs and are never executed as host actions
guards, timers, parallel state regions, hierarchy, nondeterminism, and arbitrary expressions are not supported
a replay proves the declared transition path only; it does not prove gameplay balance, user experience, or external side effects
maximum 256 states, 4096 transitions, and 10000 replay events

truth.basis: Only explicitly declared state/event transitions are applied; missing transitions HOLD and returned effects are labeled unexecuted.

agency.basis: The caller supplies the complete graph, current state, events, replay choice, and any later host interpretation of inert effects.

continuity.basis: The normalized machine and digest accompany compile, step, and replay results, preserving the exact rule body used.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: Nondeterministic transition collisions, unknown states, malformed JSON effects, and excessive graphs or replays are rejected instead of guessed through.
